_about: The only place performance budget numbers live (docs/RELEASE_STANDARD.md, section 2). tools/perf_check.py compares its medians with 'budgets' and exits 1 when a figure is over. After each improvement, lower a budget to the new figure plus 15%. Raise one only with a stated reason in the pull request.
reference_machine: Recommended spec: 8 cores, 16 GB, managed, Defender on. No named laptop yet (#121), so these budgets come from the development laptop and are provisional until the reference laptop is measured.

baseline.tool: tools/perf_check.py --quick (1 run, 20 s settle, 60 s windows). startup_s is imports plus window creation until the meeting list has rendered; interpreter start and opening the workspace are not included.
baseline.machine: Intel Core Ultra 7 255H, 16 logical processors, 31.4 GB, Windows 11 (10.0.26200), WebView2 155.0.4283.45, mains power. Deviations from section 2: Performance power plan rather than Balanced, and other apps and WebView2 windows running.

targets._about: Where the ratchet is heading (#124). CPU and start-up targets are proposals to confirm on the reference laptop. Private-bytes targets are not set yet. The #124 proposal (350 MB visible, 250 MB minimised) came before any private-bytes measurement; the first baseline is about 760 MB across 8 processes, most of it WebView2, so the targets wait for the reference laptop.

_budget_notes.minimised: Not lowered by R8 (#129), on purpose. Single quick runs on this busy development laptop on 16 Oct 2026 put minimised CPU within noise of main (R8 0.208 and 0.338% of one core; main 0.365 and 0.547%), so ratcheting on them would cause false failures. The repeatable gain was working memory: a private working set of about 70 MB minimised against about 203 MB on main. Private bytes did not change (about 755 MB), because suspending trims working memory, not commit. What CPU remains when minimised is mostly the Python side's one-second loops (R7, #128). Re-ratchet from a median of three runs on the reference laptop.
_budget_notes.worker: A fixed criterion, not a ratchet: the worker's idle unload time (120 s, workspace/worker.py) plus 5 s.
_budget_notes.leak: A fixed criterion from #124: at most 10 MB growth over 30 minutes idle (run with --leak-minutes 30). Not yet measured.
